questions.question: The __________ degree photos or videos are visuals in which the view in every direction is captured and presented simultaneously.
questions.explanation: 360-degree cameras capture spherical video/images covering all directions simultaneously.

questions.question: In Room Scale based VR Locomotion, user is teleported immediately to target location.
questions.explanation: In room-scale VR, the user physically walks around in their real space to move in the virtual space. Teleportation is a separate locomotion technique to cover larger distances.

questions.question: The __________ games are sold to user with a given price. So, user has to pay to play the game.
questions.explanation: Premium games require an upfront payment to purchase and download them.

questions.question: __________ is essentially the process by which a color is removed from an image. For example: Green Screens.
questions.explanation: Chroma Keying involves isolating and removing a specific color (usually green or blue) to replace it with a background image or video.

questions.question: The __________ refers to when a collection of 2D sprites or layers of sprites are made to move independently to create a sense of added depth (simulated Z-depth).
questions.explanation: Parallax scrolling moves background layers slower than foreground layers, creating an illusion of depth in 2D games.

questions.question: The length of __________ vector is always one unit.
questions.explanation: A normalized vector (unit vector) has a length of exactly 1.

questions.question: In game loop, the __________ phase is responsible for detecting input from user (such as keyboard and mouse).
questions.explanation: The three phases of a game loop are: Process Input, Update World, and Render Output.

questions.question: The __________ map is useful to create large 2D scenes that contain repeatable drawing patterns (shapes).
questions.explanation: Tilemaps use small, reusable image squares (tiles) to construct large game environments efficiently.

questions.question: In isometric projection, the angle between each of the three axes is __________.
questions.explanation: An isometric projection shows three dimensions with 120 degrees of separation between the projected axes.

questions.question: The __________ is the part of the animation software that represents the animation's progress over time.
questions.explanation: The timeline displays frames sequentially, indicating how properties change over time.

questions.question: The magnetic motion capture uses __________ placed on an actor's body that measure magnetic fields created by a transmitter.
questions.explanation: Magnetic motion capture tracking systems employ sensors to measure position and orientation relative to a transmitter source.

questions.question: The rule of __________ is a method of breaking up an image or design into different sections using columns and rows that form a grid.
questions.explanation: The Rule of Thirds divides a composition into a 3x3 grid, aligning key subjects along the gridlines or intersections.

questions.question: In three point lighting theory, the fill light typically has __________ the light intensity of the key light.
questions.explanation: The fill light softens shadows created by the key light and is generally set to half or lower intensity.

questions.question: A tilt is a rotation of the camera __________.
questions.explanation: Tilt tilts the camera up and down (vertical rotation); Pan turns it left and right (horizontal).

questions.question: The 3D __________ face has only 4 vertices.
questions.explanation: A Quad face is composed of 4 vertices, a triangle has 3, and an N-gon has 5 or more.

questions.question: The __________ modeling uses the operations of union, intersection and difference to change the geometry of a shape.
questions.explanation: Boolean operations combine solid models using set theory operations (union, intersect, subtract).

questions.question: In UV mapping, the coordinates U and V are normalized and range from 0 to __________.
questions.explanation: UV texture coordinates map points on a 3D model to coordinates in 2D textures ranging from 0.0 to 1.0.

questions.question: __________ mapping uses RGB values to control the surface normal components (X, Y, Z) and create the illusion of fake depth.
questions.explanation: Normal maps encode normal vectors as color channels (R=X, G=Y, B=Z) to modify lighting response.

questions.question: When an object's position is calculated relative to the position of another object, it is called __________.
questions.explanation: Relative positioning defines coordinates in reference to a parent or target object's system.

questions.question: The size of an 8-bit color depth image is __________ the size of a 24-bit image of the same resolution.
questions.explanation: 8 bits is 1 byte, while 24 bits is 3 bytes. Thus, the storage size is 1/3 of the 24-bit equivalent.

questions.question: When the image contains large areas of uniform color, it is recommended to use the __________ format.
questions.explanation: GIF/PNG are lossless formats ideal for sharp lines and flat colors, while JPEG is designed for smooth gradients in photos.

questions.question: In additive color models (like RGB), mixing two colors results in a __________.
questions.explanation: Additive mixing combines light waves, which increases total light energy and produces a brighter color.

questions.question: The subset of colors which can be accurately represented within a given color space or by a certain output device is called the __________.
questions.explanation: The gamut of an output device is the complete subset of colors that it can accurately reproduce.

questions.question: Saturation ranges from 0 to 100%. When saturation is 0%, the color becomes __________.
questions.explanation: At 0% saturation, there is no chromatic color component left, resulting in grayscale (grey/white/black).

questions.question: In color harmony schemes, choosing three colors that lie close together on the color wheel is called __________.
questions.explanation: Analogous colors are adjacent to each other on the color wheel (e.g. Red, Red-Orange, Orange).

questions.question: A __________ is created by adding black to a base hue.
questions.explanation: Shade = Hue + Black. Tint = Hue + White. Tone = Hue + Grey.

questions.question: A rigid body transformation that moves objects without deformation is __________.
questions.explanation: Rigid body transformations preserve shapes and lengths (Translation and Rotation).

questions.question: In some systems, negative values can be specified for the scaling parameters, this results in __________.
questions.explanation: A negative scaling factor reflects the coordinates across the respective axis.

questions.question: A reflection about the line x = 0 (the y-axis) flips __________ coordinates while keeping __________ coordinates the same.
questions.explanation: Reflection across the y-axis changes (x, y) to (-x, y), thereby flipping the X coordinates while keeping Y constant.

questions.question: A transformation that distorts the shape of an object, like sliding layers over each other, is called __________.
questions.explanation: Shearing slants objects in one direction by an offset proportional to their distance along the other axis.

questions.question: The need to compress media data is motivated by __________.
questions.explanation: Compression makes files smaller for disk storage and enables faster transfer speeds over networks.

questions.question: Compression can be considered as a science.
questions.explanation: Information theory, coding, and signal processing form the scientific basis of data compression.

questions.question: __________ irrelevancy occurs when the image sample density exceeds the limits of visual acuity.
questions.explanation: Visual irrelevancy represents details in an image that the human eye cannot perceive under normal viewing conditions.

questions.question: The image signal has statistical redundancy.
questions.explanation: Adjacent pixels in an image tend to have similar values, meaning there is spatial redundancy that can be compressed.

questions.question: Entropy represents the average amount of information contained per symbol in the source S.
questions.explanation: Entropy (H) measures the absolute minimum bits needed on average to encode messages from a source.

questions.question: Given a picture that has an equal distribution of black and white pixels, where probabilities are P1=0.5 and P2=0.5, the entropy H is __________.
LZW uses fixed-length codewords to represent variable-length strings of symbols/characters that commonly occur together.
questions.explanation: LZW builds a dictionary mapping variable-length strings to fixed-size indexes (typically 12 bits).

questions.question: Computer vision is concerned with the theory for building artificial systems that obtain information from images.
questions.explanation: Computer vision aims to extract meaning, interpretations, or 3D geometry from digital images/videos.

questions.question: A popular form of collision representation for humanoid characters in video games is a:
questions.explanation: Capsules are widely preferred for humanoid characters because they fit tall, standing shapes well and slide smoothly off walls.

questions.question: Markerless/Location-based AR aligns virtual objects with the real world using device sensors, which typically include:
questions.explanation: Location-based AR relies on device sensors (GPS, compass, gyroscope) and visual tracking algorithms like SLAM.

questions.question: Which game developer role is responsible for creating the soundtrack, sound effects, and voice overs?
questions.explanation: Audio engineers manage all sound assets, ambient sounds, soundtracks, and dialogue tracks.

questions.question: Scaling factors with absolute values less than 1 move points __________ the coordinate origin.
questions.explanation: Scaling factors |s| < 1 compress coordinates, bringing them closer to the center of scaling (origin).

questions.question: What is the maximum number of colors that can be defined in a standard 8-bit indexed color palette (LUT)?
questions.explanation: An 8-bit index can address up to 2^8 = 256 unique colors in a Lookup Table.

questions.question: In the HSV color model, Value (V) represents the brightness of the color and ranges from 0 to __________.
questions.explanation: HSV channels are: Hue (0-360°), Saturation (0-100%), and Value (0-100%).

questions.question: What is 'delta time' in game programming?

options.A: The time of the current frame relative to system boot
options.B: The elapsed game time since the last frame
options.C: The fixed refresh rate of the display monitor

questions.explanation: Delta time measures frame duration, allowing movement calculations to be normalized for framerate independence.

questions.question: Independent video games, most often created without publisher financial support, are called:
questions.explanation: Indie (Independent) games are developed by small teams or individuals without corporate backing.

questions.question: Architectural drawings with no distance distortion (parallel projection) are presented using:
questions.explanation: Orthographic projections preserve relative dimensions and lines remain parallel, preventing distance distortion.

questions.question: We perform __________ on a single coordinate point by adding offsets to its coordinates to generate a new coordinate position.
questions.explanation: Translation moves coordinates linearly: x' = x + tx, y' = y + ty.

questions.question: What is the least immersive implementation level of virtual reality technology?
questions.explanation: Non-immersive VR renders a 3D scene on a standard 2D flat monitor without full sensory enclosing.

questions.question: A collection of 2D vertices, edges, and faces that define the shape of a 3D object is called a:
questions.explanation: Meshes use connected vertex lists to model the outer surface shell of 3D objects.

questions.question: Imaginary bounding shapes around game objects used to determine collision detection are called:
questions.explanation: Hitboxes define bounding boundaries (often rectangular or circular) for fast overlap calculations.

questions.question: Moving a camera forward or backward, toward or away from the subject, is known as:
questions.explanation: Dolly refers to moving the camera rig physically closer or further away.

questions.question: The subset of colors which can be accurately represented within a given color space or by a certain output device is the color __________.
questions.explanation: A gamut defines the range of colors a monitor or printer is physically capable of reproducing.

questions.question: What term describes the perceived achromatic intensity of a reflecting object?
questions.explanation: Lightness (or brightness) measures perceived intensity independently of chromaticity (hue/saturation).

questions.question: A rendering issue in 3D graphics where multiple objects fight to be rendered closest to the camera due to depth precision limits is called:
questions.explanation: Z-fighting occurs when coplanar polygons have identical or near-identical Z-values, causing rendering glitches.

questions.question: Color depth in computer graphics is defined as the:

options.A: Number of pixels in an image
options.B: Number of bits used to represent each pixel's color

questions.explanation: Color depth (bit depth) determines the variety of unique colors available (e.g. 24-bit depth supports 16.7M colors).

questions.question: A 2D vector graphic representation is highly advantageous because it:

options.A: Uses a grid of pixels to store details
options.B: Can be easily scaled without resolution loss

questions.explanation: Vectors store mathematical paths (points, lines) rather than pixels, enabling infinite scaling.

questions.question: A transformation that distorts the shape of an object by shifting parallel layers relative to each other is:
questions.explanation: Shearing shifts coordinates proportionally to their distance from a parallel axis: x' = x + sh_x * y.

questions.question: Which of the following is true for vector subtraction?

options.B: It finds the displacement vector (distance and direction) between two points

questions.explanation: Subtracting vector A from B yields the displacement vector from A to B.

questions.question: What is the ratio of an image's width to its height?
questions.explanation: Aspect ratio is expressed as width:height (e.g., 16:9 or 4:3).

questions.question: What does vector addition help compute in game physics engines?
questions.explanation: Adding velocity vectors to position vectors updates object locations over time.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the HTML5 <canvas> is true?

options.A: Canvas content forms individual nodes in the DOM tree
options.B: Canvas graphics are drawn programmatically using a JavaScript API
options.C: Canvas shapes can be styled directly using CSS vector rules

questions.explanation: Canvas is a single element providing a pixel grid drawn using JS API calls.

questions.question: What does the Canvas function strokeText('Hello', 50, 50); do?

options.B: Draws the outline of text characters

questions.explanation: strokeText outlines the text; fillText fills it with color.

questions.question: What is the type name of images with 24-bit color depth?
questions.explanation: 24-bit depth allocates 8 bits each for Red, Green, and Blue, creating True Color.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a valid transformation method in the HTML5 Canvas API?
questions.explanation: Canvas supports translate, rotate, and scale. Skew is not a standard method; shear is done via transform().

questions.question: Which of these is a raster graphics file format?
questions.explanation: PNG stores images as arrays of pixels (raster), while SVG stores paths (vector).

questions.question: The term rendering in computer graphics refers to:

options.B: The process of converting 3D geometric descriptions into a 2D image

questions.explanation: Rendering calculates light interactions to translate virtual 3D models into flat screen pixels.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of Z-buffering?

options.C: Resolving visibility and occlusion of overlapping polygons

questions.explanation: Z-buffer stores the depth of each pixel to ensure objects closer to the camera obscure those behind them.

questions.question: What is the output result of a cross product between two 3D vectors?

options.C: A vector perpendicular to both input vectors

questions.explanation: The cross product of two vectors yields a third vector orthogonal to their plane.

questions.question: Which color model is often used in professional photography for a wider gamut representation?
questions.explanation: Adobe RGB offers a larger green-cyan gamut than sRGB, which is preferred for photography.

questions.question: What is delta time used for in game loops?

options.B: Making game physics updates frame-rate independent

questions.explanation: Multiplying physics movements by delta time ensures objects move at the same speed regardless of frames per second.

questions.question: What is 'Lightness' (L) in the HSL model and how does it differ from 'Value' (V) in HSV?

options.A: L is the average of RGB max and min components, whereas V is simply the maximum RGB component
options.B: L is the intensity of red light, whereas V is blue light
options.C: There is no difference between them

questions.explanation: L in HSL is calculated as (max + min)/2, giving a symmetric scale for brightness, whereas V in HSV is max(R,G,B).

questions.question: What is a shear transformation primarily used for in graphics?

options.C: Sliding parallel layers of an object relative to one another

questions.explanation: Shear shifts coordinates along one direction by an amount proportional to the other coordinate.

questions.question: What is the difference between stroke() and fill() in the HTML5 Canvas API?

options.A: stroke() outlines the path; fill() fills the path interior
options.B: stroke() fills the path; fill() only outlines it
options.C: They perform the exact same action

questions.explanation: fill() renders solid colors inside shapes; stroke() draws lines along shape outlines.

questions.question: What size matrix is standard for representing 3D transformations?
questions.explanation: 3D translation and projection require 4x4 matrices in homogeneous coordinates.

questions.question: What does anti-aliasing improve in an image?

options.B: Visual smoothness by reducing jagged edges (jaggies)
options.C: The resolution of the source asset

questions.explanation: Anti-aliasing blends edge pixels with background colors to soften stair-step distortion.

questions.question: Which of the following is an additive color model used in digital displays?
questions.explanation: Displays mix Red, Green, and Blue light beams (additive) to create colors.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of vector graphics over raster graphics?
questions.explanation: Vectors scale infinitely without pixelation because they use mathematical primitives.

questions.question: How many bits are needed to encode 16 quantization levels in an analog-to-digital converter (ADC)?
questions.explanation: 2^4 = 16. Thus, 4 bits are required to represent 16 distinct quantization levels.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a primary color in the additive RGB color model?
questions.explanation: Yellow is a secondary color in RGB (created by Red + Green light) but a primary in CMY subtractive models.

questions.question: In which aspect can Data Visualization assist researchers?
questions.explanation: Data visualization aids in raw exploration, pattern detection, analysis, and final presentation of metrics.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the closePath() function in the Canvas API?

options.B: Draws a straight line from the current point back to the start of the current sub-path

questions.explanation: closePath() closes a path loop by connecting the end point back to the origin of that path segment.

questions.question: If scaling factors Sx, Sy, and Sz are equal in 3D transformations, it is called:
questions.explanation: Uniform scaling scales all dimensions by the same ratio, preserving object proportions.

questions.question: What is the smallest addressable unit in a raster image?
questions.explanation: A pixel (picture element) is the smallest physical point in a raster image grid.

questions.question: Which operation is considered a rigid-body transformation?
questions.explanation: Rotation and translation preserve distances and shapes, making them rigid-body transforms.

questions.question: What is a vector commonly used for in 2D/3D game programming?

options.B: Storing positions, directions, and velocities of entities

questions.explanation: Vectors represent direction and magnitude, ideal for tracking positions and movements in space.

questions.question: Which geometric shape is commonly used for basic hitboxes in 2D games?
questions.explanation: Circles and axis-aligned boxes (rectangles) are used for simple, high-performance collision checks.

questions.question: Which process converts a graphical primitive's geometric definition into pixel coordinates?
questions.explanation: Scan conversion decides which screen pixels correspond to lines, circles, or polygons.

questions.question: In the RGB color model, what color is produced by mixing red and green at full intensity?
questions.explanation: Red light + Green light = Yellow light (additive mixing).

questions.question: What is an infographic?

options.B: A visual representation of information in a graphic format

questions.explanation: Infographics combine text, icons, and diagrams to present complex data clearly.

questions.question: What is the default width and height of an HTML5 <canvas> element if not specified?
questions.explanation: By default, the canvas element is initialized to a width of 300 pixels and height of 150 pixels.

questions.question: In Bresenham's line-drawing algorithm for slope m < 1, what coordinates are plotted next if decision parameter p < 0?
questions.explanation: For p < 0, the next pixel chosen is the East pixel, meaning x is incremented by 1 and y remains unchanged.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the <canvas> element in HTML5?
questions.explanation: Canvas acts as a scriptable container to draw dynamic lines, shapes, and pixel buffers on the fly.

questions.question: The basic task of __________ is to generate image by geometry description of objects in 3D space.
questions.explanation: Rendering converts a 3D scene description (geometry, lights, materials) into a 2D image.

questions.question: In the RGB color model, combining red and blue light at full intensity produces:
questions.explanation: Additive mixing: Red + Blue = Magenta. Red + Green = Yellow. Green + Blue = Cyan.

questions.question: The DDA (Digital Differential Analyzer) line-drawing algorithm calculates the number of steps as:
questions.explanation: DDA steps along the dominant axis (larger absolute difference), iterating max(|Δx|, |Δy|) times.

questions.question: In Bresenham's circle drawing algorithm, the initial decision parameter p0 for radius r is:
questions.explanation: The midpoint circle algorithm starts with p0 = 1 − r. When p < 0 choose East, else choose South-East.

questions.question: Which 2D transformation uses homogeneous coordinates to enable matrix multiplication of all transforms?
questions.explanation: Translation is NOT linear (cannot be expressed as a 2×2 matrix), but homogeneous 3×3 matrices allow translation to be combined with rotation and scaling.

questions.question: Reflecting a point (x, y) across the line y = x gives:
questions.explanation: Reflection in the line y = x simply swaps the x and y coordinates.

questions.question: When the scaling factor is negative (e.g. Sx = −1, Sy = 1), the result is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: Sx = −1 negates the x-coordinates, which is identical to reflecting across the y-axis.

questions.question: Boundary-fill and flood-fill are two common algorithms for:
questions.explanation: Both algorithms fill a closed region starting from an interior seed point.

questions.question: Which fill algorithm stops when it reaches a pixel matching the boundary color?
questions.explanation: Boundary-fill expands from a seed point until it hits pixels of the specified boundary color.

questions.question: The process of spreading a histogram uniformly across all intensity levels to improve contrast is called:
questions.explanation: Histogram equalization remaps intensities using the cumulative distribution function (CDF) to produce a flat histogram.

questions.question: A 3×3 mean (box) filter applied to an image produces a:
questions.explanation: Averaging neighboring pixels suppresses high-frequency detail, producing blur/smoothing.

questions.question: In the frequency domain, a low-pass filter is used to:
questions.explanation: Low-pass filters retain low spatial frequencies (smooth regions) and suppress high frequencies (edges/noise).

questions.question: Augmented Reality (AR) differs from Virtual Reality (VR) in that AR:

options.A: Replaces the real world with a virtual one
options.B: Overlays digital content onto the real world

questions.explanation: AR augments the real environment with virtual objects; VR replaces it entirely.

questions.question: Which AR type uses physical printed images or QR codes to align virtual objects?
questions.explanation: Marker-based AR (e.g. ARToolKit) detects a predefined 2D marker/QR image to position 3D objects.

questions.question: SLAM stands for:
questions.explanation: SLAM builds a map of an unknown environment while simultaneously tracking the device's location within it — key to markerless AR.

questions.question: Computer Vision is primarily concerned with:

options.B: Interpreting and extracting meaning from images

questions.explanation: CV enables machines to understand visual information (classification, detection, segmentation).

questions.question: Which computer vision task assigns a single label to an entire input image?
questions.explanation: Classification outputs one global label (e.g. 'cat') for the whole image, unlike detection or segmentation.

questions.question: The Sobel operator is commonly used in computer vision for:
questions.explanation: Sobel computes image gradients to highlight intensity transitions, used as an edge detector.

questions.question: In CMY color model, the formula to convert from RGB is:

options.A: C = R, M = G, Y = B
options.C: C = R+G, M = G+B, Y = B+R

questions.explanation: CMY is the subtractive complement of RGB: C = 1−R, M = 1−G, Y = 1−B.

questions.question: In raster graphics, a frame buffer stores:

options.A: Vector path commands for each object
options.B: Color values for every pixel on the screen

questions.explanation: The frame buffer is a block of memory holding the RGB (or RGBA) color value of each screen pixel.

questions.question: Computer Graphics is concerned with:

options.B: Generating and manipulating images using computers

questions.explanation: CG focuses on creating, modifying, and rendering visual content programmatically.

questions.question: If two vectors are perpendicular, their dot product is:
questions.explanation: The dot product of two orthogonal vectors is 0 because cos(90°) = 0.

questions.question: The result of calling LERP(start, end, 0.5) is:

options.C: The midpoint between start and end

questions.explanation: LERP(a, b, t) = a + t*(b−a). At t = 0.5 it returns the midpoint.

questions.question: The game loop consists of three phases. Which of the following correctly completes: 'Input Processing, __________ World, Generate Output'?
questions.explanation: The three canonical game loop phases are: Process Input → Update World → Generate Output.

questions.question: A __________ is a 2D visual object (image) in the game world used to represent characters or background elements.
questions.explanation: Sprites are 2D bitmap images rendered in a game scene, commonly used for characters and UI.

questions.question: When a design contains many repeating patterns, it is best to use a __________ map.
questions.explanation: Tilemaps use a grid of small reusable tiles to efficiently build large, repetitive environments.

questions.question: In the DDA line algorithm, the number of steps required equals:
questions.explanation: DDA uses the larger difference to ensure no gaps appear in the drawn line.

questions.question: In isometric projection, the angle between each of the three projected axes is:
questions.explanation: Isometric projection spaces the X, Y, and Z axes equally at 120° apart.

questions.question: Which raster image format supports lossless compression?
questions.explanation: PNG uses the DEFLATE lossless compression algorithm, preserving all pixel data exactly.

questions.question: If an image has an original size of 200×Y pixels and is scaled to 100×400 pixels while maintaining the same aspect ratio, what is Y?
questions.explanation: Aspect ratio preserved: 200/Y = 100/400 → Y = 200 × 400 / 100 = 800 pixels.

questions.question: In the RGB color model, which primary color combination produces white light?
questions.explanation: All three additive primaries at maximum intensity combine to produce white (255, 255, 255).

questions.question: The Hue component in the HSV/HSL model represents:

options.B: The angle on the color wheel (0–360°) indicating color type

questions.explanation: Hue is the perceived color attribute (e.g. 0° = red, 120° = green, 240° = blue).

questions.question: Translation in 2D moves a point P(x, y) by offsets (tx, ty). The result is:
questions.explanation: Translation adds the displacement vector to each coordinate: x' = x + tx, y' = y + ty.

questions.question: Applying a rotation by 90° CCW to point (1, 0) gives:
Region-filling algorithms begin from a __________ point inside the region.
questions.explanation: Flood-fill and boundary-fill both start at an interior seed pixel and expand outward.

questions.question: 8-way connected fill includes diagonal neighbors. Compared to 4-way connectivity, 8-way fill:
questions.explanation: 8-connectivity checks all 8 neighbors per pixel, allowing fill to propagate through diagonal gaps.

questions.question: Augmented Reality overlays digital information onto the real world. Which sensor type is essential for markerless AR location tracking?
questions.explanation: GPS provides geographic location; accelerometer tracks device orientation and motion for markerless AR.

questions.question: Non-immersive Virtual Reality typically involves:

options.C: A standard computer monitor and input devices

questions.explanation: Non-immersive VR presents a virtual world on a desktop screen; the user is not surrounded by the virtual environment.

questions.question: In image processing, applying a high-pass filter to an image will:
questions.explanation: High-pass filters remove low-frequency (smooth) components, leaving behind high-frequency edges and details.

questions.question: In the convolution theorem, spatial-domain convolution is equivalent to __________ in the frequency domain.
questions.explanation: The convolution theorem states: f * g in spatial domain ↔ F × G in frequency domain. This is why frequency-domain filtering is computationally efficient.
